rationale: A coherent generalization of the archive's best flow signal into a net-payout-to-capital measure, but it is close to the known net-external-financing anomaly, it retains the negative-gross-profit denominator inversion the proposal set elsewhere admits is a defect, and it enters dvc with the opposite sign to the two archived dividend-gated signals without reconciling that tension.

This is a pure horizon-tuning variant of CheapDeleveragingFromProfits — one operator argument changed — which is exactly the cosmetic re-parameterization the objective asks researchers to avoid, and its diagnostic value does not justify a full evaluation slot.

Value-gated net share issuance is a thin wrapper on the well-documented net-stock-issuance/composite-issuance anomaly, and the construction is mechanically flawed because raw DELTA(csho) is contaminated by splits and stock dividends and the gross-profit denominator flips sign for loss-making cheap firms.

The denominator swap is motivated by a real and correctly diagnosed inversion in the gross-profit-scaled burden family, making it a legitimate robustness test rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the grading leg reduces to a fairly standard capital-intensity/leverage measure and the expected incremental insight is modest.

The stated mechanism is undermined by the arithmetic: raw operating earnings yield has an order of magnitude more cross-sectional dispersion than the effective borrowing rate, so the signal will be dominated by plain E/P — a canonical value anomaly — contradicting the claim that neither leg carries the signal, and zero-debt firms make the promised "full coverage" false.

A sensible test of whether the dividend gate's reliable alphas come from payout safety or general earning power, and the revenue scaling avoids the negative-denominator problem, but the archived dividend-gated signals all show strong alphas with null Fama-MacBeth slopes, so this likely reinherits a gate-driven, grading-leg-independent result.
